citation: Hartley's studio, West Madison Street, Chicago, multigraph photograph of Frances Macbeth Glessner: five views of her taken at once in two mirrors set at about 75 degrees, about February 1897. Glessner House collection, reproduced in 'The many sides of Frances Glessner', The Story of a House (Glessner House blog), 9 February 2015.
author: Hartley's (studio), Chicago
repository: Glessner House, Chicago (the museum's collection, as the blog post says). The copy used here, 675 x 375 px, was supplied by the owner on 2026-11-07 and is held in kevinrhaas/chicago-evidence at evidence/people-portraits-2026-11-07/glessner_frances_m/.
locator: The whole print: from left, her left profile, a three-quarter front, the back of her head, a three-quarter front turned the other way, and her right profile.
rights_note: A photograph made in 1897 is out of copyright in the United States. The original belongs to Glessner House; credit Glessner House, Chicago.
access_notes: Read on 2026-11-07 (T-3473) from the blog post, which quotes her journal: she went to Hartley's on West Madison Street and had her photograph taken, a multigraph; the sitter faced two mirrors at about 75 degrees, giving five views on one negative. The blog's own image was not fetched; the owner supplied the copy.
note: Frances Glessner at 49, seen five ways at once: in a dark silk bodice with large puffed sleeves, a high black collar and a lace front, her dark hair drawn up to a crown of thick braids with a bow at the nape. The two profiles and the back view show the shape of her head and how her hair was dressed, which the 1892 conservatory photograph cannot.
what_it_supplies: the profile of her face and the shape of her head from the side and back, as a cross-check on the fitted face
how she dressed her hair in 1897: drawn up to a crown of braids
what_it_does_not_supply: marks fine enough to fit (the heads are about 60 px high in the copy held)
